finding: the index's per-month byte size (entry.velikostDumpu) is printed and stored into state.months[k].bytes but never compared to the received byte count; a server that advertises and delivers a smaller total is marked done. The runtime's fetch already fails a short body under a truthful Content-Length and stops at the header's length on an oversized body, so those two checks are made by the transport, not by the script. Short-body failure leaves a truncated file at the FINAL name (retry rewrites it).

seam_notes: Sidecar `<pdf>.txt` beside the bytes; line 1 is `#parsed-text/1 unpdf@<version> sha256:<16>` — format version, parser identity+version and a source fingerprint, all three required to match. A missing/older/foreign stamp is a loud miss, never a silent pass; an unreadable unpdf version disables the sidecar rather than degrading it to an unverifiable cache (absent-guard-is-loud). Written .part-then-rename; deleteParsedText() is the reaper. Gate green: npm run typecheck clean, unit lane lib/ingest 228/228 (8 new). Second ingest: unpdf invocations 1 -> 0 per PDF, i.e. 23 -> 0 for the slice.
falsifier: Wall time is not the payoff. Measured on this box: 23 parses of a synthetic 55-line posting PDF = 104,7 ms vs 1,6 ms of sidecar reads. The real .justice-samples/ corpus is gitignored and absent from every checkout, so the proposal T1 timing could not be run at all. If the payoff has to be seconds, this is not worth its coherence surface; it is worth it only for the other two forces — re-scoring the corpus when unpdf is absent or bumped, and attributing a diff to the extractor change rather than to a silent re-parse. Divergence from the proposal: it copied LightRAG warn-never-reparse; a version mismatch here re-parses and re-stamps, because warn-never-reparse leaves the corpus permanently mixed (new PDFs still enter at the new engine) while re-parse converges it.
